clue.text: Old boy in race — one badly needing oxygen

indicators.note: the old boy's letters are placed inside the jumbled letters
done badly, the letters of race and one are put in a muddled order

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
OB is the standard abbreviation for an old boy of a school

explanation.surface: A former pupil running a race, gasping for breath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'race' looks like the running event, but it is anagram fodder; 'needing oxygen' is the definition, describing exercise or organisms.
explanation.definitionFit: Aerobic exercise or organisms depend on a supply of oxygen to function.

clue.text: Impressive time for a Roman Emperor, but not us

indicators.note: but not means the following letters are taken away

parts.note: Augustus was the first Roman emperor

explanation.surface: A grand era for Rome's ruler, but not for the rest of us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'time for' adds a second hint: the month named after the emperor.
explanation.definitionFit: August means grand, venerable and awe-inspiring.

clue.text: Such a colourful exhibition may be above us

definitions.text: Such a colourful exhibition may be above us

parts.words: Such a colourful exhibition may be above us
parts.note: the colourful display seems like a gallery show, but is a band of colours in the sky after rain

explanation.surface: A vivid art show could be over our heads.
explanation.definitionFit: A bow of spectral colours appears in the sky when sun shines through rain.

clue.text: Raised gallery whence you can view Apollo, perhaps

definitions.text: Raised gallery whence you can view

explanation.surface: A viewing gallery from which a famous statue can be admired.
explanation.walkthrough: The Apollo Belvedere is a famous classical statue in the Vatican.
explanation.definitionFit: A belvedere is a raised turret or summerhouse with a fine view, and the Apollo statue bears the name.

clue.text: Came to spend freely, getting repaid

indicators.note: freely means the letters of came to spend are arranged without constraint

explanation.surface: Someone arrived to spend lavishly and got paid back.
explanation.definitionFit: Compensated means reimbursed or recompensed for a loss.

clue.text: Bishop a Jew rejected early on

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a Jew is a Semite

explanation.surface: A bishop turning away a Jewish man at an early hour.
explanation.walkthrough: A Jew is a Semite, a member of the Semitic peoples; 'early on' defines an old-fashioned adverb.
explanation.definitionFit: Betimes is an old-fashioned adverb meaning in good time, at an early hour.

clue.text: Opener, perhaps, for serving up tongue

indicators.note: in a down clue serving up means the word is read upwards

parts.note: a tab is a small flap or tongue of material

explanation.surface: A waiter serving a tongue dish as a starter.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an opener is a batsman, a bat, who goes in first.
explanation.definitionFit: An opening batsman is a bat in cricket slang.

clue.text: Out, thanks to barracking

parts.note: ta is British slang for thanks
barracking is jeering, booing

explanation.surface: Sent off, thanks to a jeering crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: Something taboo is banned, socially off-limits.

clue.text: Command also accepted by the first officer

indicators.note: accepted by means the also word is taken inside the officer word

parts.note: the mate is the first officer on a merchant ship
and means also

explanation.surface: An order also taken on board by a ship's officer.
explanation.definitionFit: A mandate is an official order or authority to act.

clue.text: Wine may thus, go round, some say

indicators.note: some say means the pieces are heard rather than spelt

parts.note: so means thus; to turn is to go round

explanation.surface: Wine may make your head spin, as some claim.
explanation.walkthrough: SO TURN said aloud sounds like the wine; 'may' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Sauterne is a sweet white dessert wine from Bordeaux.

clue.text: Bird returned book after breather outside University

indicators.note: the turned book follows the breather in the answer
the breathing organ's letters go round the letter for university

parts.note: a gill is the organ a fish breathes with

indicators.note: returned means brought back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a tome is a large book

explanation.surface: A bird gives back a library book after a breathing break outside college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breather' is not a rest but a fish's breathing organ; U sits inside it after the G, and the turned book follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A guillemot is a black-and-white seabird of the auk family that nests on cliffs.

clue.text: African appears to forbid familiarity in France

parts.note: to ban is to forbid
tu is the familiar French word for you, used between intimates

explanation.surface: An African visitor seems to frown on over-familiar address in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appears to' is a link joining definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bantu are a large family of peoples across central and southern Africa.

clue.text: Runs through Southern president with a sword

indicators.note: runs passing through puts its letter within the other pieces

parts.note: Abe is Abraham Lincoln, the US president
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Someone runs a Confederate leader through with a blade.
explanation.walkthrough: R goes 'through' S plus ABE, landing between B and E; 'with a' links.
explanation.definitionFit: A sabre is a heavy cavalry blade with a curved edge.

clue.text: Oriental dined outside American work complex

indicators.note: the eastern letter and the dining word sit around the American work word

parts.note: E stands for east, the Orient
ate means dined
labor is the American spelling of labour, work

explanation.surface: An Eastern diner eats away from an American factory site.
explanation.walkthrough: E plus ATE goes 'outside' LABOR, the US spelling, giving E-LABOR-ATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Elaborate means intricate and involved, with many detailed parts.

clue.text: Notice vehicle sticker — it's a form of promotion

parts.note: an ad is a notice in a paper
a van is a vehicle
cement is something that sticks things together

explanation.surface: A vehicle sticker as an advert campaign.
explanation.definitionFit: Advancement is moving up in rank or status, as in a promotion.

clue.text: Beautiful age for fruit, perhaps — even in a Dutch painter

parts.note: fruit can be served as a sweet, a dessert course

indicators.note: the word even is placed inside the painter's name

parts.note: Jan Steen was a 17th-century Dutch genre painter
taken as written

explanation.surface: Admiring a mellow vintage of fruit, then praising a Dutch master.
explanation.walkthrough: Jan Steen is the Dutch painter; 'fruit, perhaps' is an example of a sweet, the dessert course.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase celebrates seventeen as a lovely time of youthful bloom.

clue.text: Chemical process for putting up the tin quota

indicators.note: in a down clue putting up means the word is read upwards

parts.note: taken as written, tin
a ration is a fixed allowance or quota

explanation.surface: A factory process for raising the tin quota.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitration is a reaction introducing a nitro group into a compound.

clue.text: Obstruction under the nail — a bit of grass

indicators.note: in a down clue under means the obstruction word comes below the nail word

parts.note: a spike is a large nail
a let is an obstruction, as in without let or hindrance

explanation.surface: A splinter under the fingernail, and a blade of grass.
explanation.definitionFit: A spikelet is a small flower cluster in grasses.

clue.text: Inescapable fate met while still travelling?

explanation.surface: Destiny meeting someone before they arrive anywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as PRE-DESTINATION, the second part describes meeting someone before reaching their journey's end.
explanation.definitionFit: Predestination is the doctrine that all is fixed in advance; split, it also describes meeting before the end of a journey.

clue.text: Observe rising boy scholar

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the word is read upwards

parts.note: to note is to observe
Ian is a boy's name

explanation.surface: Watching a boy grow into a student.
explanation.walkthrough: An Etonian is a pupil of Eton, an elite English school.
explanation.definitionFit: An Etonian is a pupil at Eton College.

clue.text: In which marching bands may strike up a tune

definitions.text: In which marching bands may strike up a tune

parts.words: In which marching bands may strike up a tune
parts.note: describes the outdoor setting where marching bands play

explanation.surface: The setting where marching bands play.
explanation.definitionFit: Outdoor events take place outside, not under a roof.

clue.text: Sustenance required before invading a state

indicators.note: invading means the before word goes inside the state word

parts.note: Cal is an abbreviation for California, a US state
ere is an archaic word for before

explanation.surface: Food supplies needed before an army invades a country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'required' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Cereal is grain food, a staple form of nourishment.

clue.text: Acquaintance in England woke without an awful shaking

indicators.note: an awful shaking churns the letters of England and woke into a new order

parts.note: these letters are what must be taken out of the mixed pool

explanation.surface: Someone in England woke up after a terrible tremor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes A and N from ENGLANDWOKE; 'awful shaking' rearranges the remaining nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Knowledge of a subject means familiarity with it, being acquainted with the facts.

clue.text: Shoot a female bird, perhaps

explanation.surface: A hunter shoots a hen bird.
explanation.walkthrough: In gardening a layer is a shoot bent into the soil to root; a laying hen is a layer.
explanation.definitionFit: A layer is a stem pegged down to root, and also a hen kept for eggs.

clue.text: Popular, if non-U, to be kept in drink

indicators.note: the be word is held inside the drink word

parts.note: ale is beer, a drink
be is the infinitive verb in to be

explanation.surface: A popular tipple, unless one is too posh to keep drinking it.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is itself wordplay: remove U from popular to get poplar, a tree. Non-U is also British slang for not upper-class.
explanation.definitionFit: An abele is the white poplar tree.

clue.text: Write a song about it for ordinary people

indicators.note: about means the song word goes around the word it

parts.note: a lay is a short narrative song or poem

explanation.surface: Composing a song for the man in the street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' tells the song to go round the other word; 'Write a' and 'for' are links, and a lay is an old narrative poem.
explanation.definitionFit: The laity are the non-clergy, everyday folk of a church.

clue.text: Make a crackling sound, but kick up about mine

indicators.note: the kick up word goes around the mine word

parts.note: to kick up a fuss is to create
a pit is a coal mine

explanation.surface: A fire crackling, but miners making a fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: CREATE goes 'about' PIT to make CRE-PIT-ATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To crepitate is to crackle or make a rattling noise.

clue.text: Backs alongside this projection?

explanation.surface: Something running beside a projecting feature.
explanation.walkthrough: The Backs are the Cambridge college lawns along the river Cam.
explanation.definitionFit: A cam is a projecting part on a rotating shaft, and the Cambridge river flows past the Backs.

clue.text: Flare-up? So much for the French spirit!

parts.note: tant is French for so much
rum is a spirit distilled from sugar cane

explanation.surface: A drinker's angry outburst at the French measure of spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: A tantrum is a sudden outburst of bad temper.

clue.text: Climber; or a number training, say

indicators.note: say means the words are heard rather than spelt

parts.note: ten is a number and drill is training

explanation.surface: A rock climber, or a group of ten doing exercises.
explanation.walkthrough: TEN DRILL said quickly sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A tendril is a thin shoot a climbing plant uses to cling to supports.
